stories.title: Siemens SIPLUS and SIMATIC Products
CISA Adds One Known Exploited Vulnerability to Catalog
Zyxel and Veeam Flaws Under Active Exploitation With Command and SYSTEM Access
New CVSS 10.0 VeloCloud Orchestrator Flaw Actively Exploited in Certificate-Based Setups
Critical Check Point Management Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Run Code as Root
NightmareEclipse's latest zero-day leaves Microsoft Defender stuck in the past
F5 security advisory (AV26-949)
D-Link warns of max severity zero-day bug in DIR-822A routers
stories.abstract: D-Link has disclosed a critical, unpatched vulnerability in its legacy DIR-822A routers. The flaw is currently exposed to public proof-of-concept exploit code, leaving these devices susceptible to remote attacks without a vendor-provided fix.
stories.why: Unpatched, publicly exploitable vulnerabilities in edge networking hardware provide attackers with easy entry points into internal networks.
stories.action: Retire or isolate affected DIR-822A routers from the internet immediately.

stories.title: Roundcube security advisory (AV26-503) – Update 1
OpenPLC Runtime v3
lwIP (Lightweight IP)
Siemens Desigo CC family
stories.abstract: Siemens Desigo CC versions V6 and V7 contain a code injection vulnerability. Attackers can exploit this by using malicious graphics documents with embedded scripts, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution on client devices and subsequent lateral movement within the network.
stories.why: This flaw allows remote attackers to compromise building management systems, providing a foothold for deeper infiltration into critical infrastructure environments.
stories.action: Contact Siemens support for patch availability and guidance on securing Desigo CC graphics configurations.

stories.title: Siemens Industrial Edge Management
stories.abstract: Siemens Industrial Edge Management platforms contain a critical authentication bypass flaw. An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit the password recovery mechanism to reset credentials and gain full control over user accounts without needing email verification.
stories.why: This vulnerability allows complete unauthorized access to industrial management infrastructure, posing a severe risk to operational technology environments.
stories.action: Update Industrial Edge Management to the latest available versions immediately.

stories.title: Muse, Meta's extraordinarily privileged AI assistant, has a serious 0-day
stories.abstract: Researchers identified a zero-day vulnerability in Meta's Muse AI agent that allows attackers to hijack the system. The flaw is susceptible to ClickFix-style exploitation, potentially granting unauthorized control over the assistant's privileged functions.
stories.why: AI agents with high-level system permissions represent a significant new attack surface for automated exploitation and unauthorized data access.

stories.title: Two arrested in UK after Microsoft takedown of ‘Eviltokens’ AI-chatbot for cybercriminals
stories.abstract: UK authorities apprehended two individuals linked to EvilTokens, a Telegram-based service that leveraged AI to automate phishing, inbox analysis, and account takeover operations. Microsoft collaborated with law enforcement to dismantle the platform, which charged monthly fees for its malicious automation capabilities.
stories.why: This highlights the growing trend of AI-as-a-service platforms lowering the barrier to entry for sophisticated account takeover and fraud campaigns.

stories.title: New Linux Kernel Flaw Gives ARM64 KVM Guests Read-Write Access to Host Memory
SharePoint Flaw Initially Listed as Spoofing by Microsoft Enables Authenticated RCE
Siemens SIMOVE Fleetmanager and SIPLANT
stories.abstract: Siemens SIMOVE Fleetmanager and SIPLANT software contain a path traversal vulnerability. This flaw allows unauthorized actors to read files outside the intended directory structure, potentially exposing sensitive system information.
stories.why: Path traversal in industrial management software can lead to unauthorized access to configuration files, credentials, or other critical system data.
stories.action: Update SIMOVE Fleetmanager and SIPLANT to the latest patched versions provided by Siemens.

stories.title: Siemens WTV676 and WTV776
Siemens Siveillance Control
stories.abstract: A critical flaw in the Open Interface Services module of Siemens Siveillance Control and Control Pro allows remote attackers to upload arbitrary files. Successful exploitation grants unauthorized root-level access to the underlying server.
stories.why: This vulnerability provides full system compromise, posing a severe risk to physical security management infrastructure.
stories.action: Update Siveillance Control and Control Pro to the latest patched versions provided by Siemens.

stories.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: Cisco 0-Day, AI Agent RCE, ClickFix Attacks, ClickFix Surge, and Browser Hijacks
2026-013: Critical Vulnerability in F5 BIG-IP APM
stories.abstract: F5 has disclosed a critical security flaw impacting the BIG-IP Access Policy Manager. The vendor reports that malicious actors are currently leveraging this vulnerability in active attacks, necessitating immediate attention from administrators to secure their infrastructure.
stories.why: Active exploitation of critical vulnerabilities in edge networking appliances poses a high risk of unauthorized access and potential system compromise.
stories.action: Apply the vendor-provided security patches immediately.

stories.title: WordPress Comment2Shell Flaw Can Turn Anonymous Comment XSS Into RCE via Admin Session
stories.abstract: A critical vulnerability in WordPress core, dubbed Comment2Shell, allows unauthenticated attackers to inject malicious scripts via comments. When an administrator views the compromised comment, the script executes, potentially granting the attacker remote code execution capabilities on the underlying server.
stories.why: This flaw enables full server compromise by leveraging administrative sessions, posing a severe risk to site integrity and data confidentiality.
stories.action: Update WordPress to version 7.1.1 or later immediately.

stories.title: Recent ZyXEL Switch Vulnerability Exploited by Chinese Hackers
stories.abstract: A Chinese-linked threat group has successfully compromised approximately 1,000 ZyXEL network switches. The attackers leveraged an undisclosed vulnerability to gain unauthorized access and exfiltrate sensitive data from the affected hardware.
stories.why: This indicates active exploitation of network infrastructure by sophisticated actors, posing a significant risk to data confidentiality and internal network integrity.

stories.title: ‘We Hacked the FBI:’ Hackers Say They Have Data on All FBI Employees
stories.abstract: Threat actors claim to have breached the FBI, leaking a dataset containing personal information for thousands of employees. The exposed records reportedly include names, residential addresses, contact details, and information regarding spouses of bureau personnel.
stories.why: This represents a significant compromise of sensitive government personnel data, posing severe physical security and social engineering risks to federal law enforcement.

stories.title: Cisco Zero-Day Highlights API Endpoint Authentication Issues
Google Fined €403 Million Over GDPR Violations Tied to Location Data
stories.abstract: Ireland's Data Protection Commission has penalized Google over 460 million dollars for violating GDPR regulations. The fine stems from a multi-year investigation into how the company managed and processed user location data between 2018 and 2020.
stories.why: This highlights ongoing regulatory scrutiny regarding user privacy and the legal risks associated with how large-scale platforms handle sensitive telemetry data.

stories.title: LausivLoader analysis, or how to pass data between malware stages, (Thu, Sep 17th)
EvilTokens PhaaS disrupted after compromising 12,000 Microsoft accounts
stories.abstract: Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit successfully dismantled the EvilTokens platform, a phishing-as-a-service operation responsible for hijacking over 12,000 Microsoft accounts across 10,000 distinct organizations by bypassing multi-factor authentication through session token theft.
stories.why: This takedown mitigates a significant source of adversary-in-the-middle attacks targeting enterprise identity providers and session-based authentication.

stories.title: The Truth about GET and HTTP Standards, (Tue, Sep 22nd)
stories.abstract: A new HTTP method called QUERY has been introduced to standardize requests that require a body, addressing the ambiguity and potential security risks associated with including bodies in traditional GET requests, which are technically permitted but often ignored or mishandled by servers.
stories.why: Standardizing request bodies prevents inconsistent parsing behavior across different web servers and proxies, which can lead to request smuggling or security bypasses.

stories.title: New WordPress Click2Shell Flaw Forces Theme Installs, Can Chain to Code Execution
stories.abstract: WordPress has addressed a vulnerability dubbed Click2Shell that allows unauthorized theme installation. By tricking an authenticated administrator into clicking a malicious link, attackers can trigger the installation of themes from the official directory, potentially leading to remote code execution.
stories.why: This flaw enables attackers to gain persistent access or execute arbitrary code by leveraging the high-level privileges of an active administrator session.
stories.action: Update WordPress core to the latest version immediately.

stories.title: MISP security advisory (AV26-946)
stories.abstract: The Cyber Centre has issued advisories for multiple software platforms. MISP versions prior to 2.5.47, various MongoDB drivers, and Exim mail server versions before 4.100.1 are impacted by security vulnerabilities requiring administrative attention and potential configuration changes.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities could allow unauthorized privilege escalation, improper data handling, or remote exploitation within critical infrastructure and mail routing environments.
stories.action: Update MISP to 2.5.47 and Exim to 4.100.1; review MongoDB driver versions for patches.

stories.title: SideCopy Broadens India Targeting to Academia With ReverseRAT Spear-Phishing
stories.abstract: The SideCopy threat group is shifting its focus toward Indian academic institutions. The attackers utilize spear-phishing lures to deploy malicious scripts, specifically abusing the mshta.exe utility to bypass traditional security controls and execute their ReverseRAT malware.
stories.why: This indicates an expansion of targeting scope for a known APT, necessitating increased scrutiny of email-based delivery vectors and living-off-the-land binary abuse.

stories.title: TASK#STOMP PowerShell Backdoor Steals Documents, Wi-Fi Passwords, and Clipboard Data
stories.abstract: A newly identified campaign, TASK#STOMP, utilizes a PowerShell backdoor to exfiltrate sensitive business documents, clipboard data, and Wi-Fi credentials. The malware maintains persistence by monitoring the filesystem for new files and supports remote command execution via screenshots and arbitrary input.
stories.why: This backdoor provides attackers with comprehensive surveillance and data exfiltration capabilities, posing a significant risk to intellectual property and internal network credentials.

stories.title: IBM security advisory (AV26-943)
stories.abstract: IBM has released security updates addressing multiple vulnerabilities across a wide range of enterprise products, including WebSphere Application Server, IBM MQ, Guardium Data Protection, and Sterling File Gateway. Administrators should review the official advisory to identify affected versions within their environments.
stories.why: These products are critical infrastructure components; unpatched vulnerabilities could lead to unauthorized access, data exposure, or remote code execution within enterprise networks.
stories.action: Review the IBM security advisory and apply the recommended patches for your specific product versions.

stories.title: BigCommerce alerts merchants of data breach linked to Ribon apps
stories.abstract: BigCommerce notified several merchants of unauthorized data access resulting from compromised third-party Ribon application credentials. Attackers leveraged these stolen credentials to inject malicious scripts directly into affected online storefronts, potentially exposing customer information.
stories.why: Supply chain attacks targeting third-party integrations bypass platform-level security, highlighting the risk of over-privileged application access in e-commerce environments.
stories.action: Audit third-party application permissions and rotate API credentials for all integrated Ribon services.

stories.title: North Korean Attackers Hit 30,000 Devices and Steal $10.7m
stories.abstract: The threat actor group WaterPlum successfully compromised 30,000 individual devices. This campaign resulted in the theft of approximately $10.7 million in assets, impacting roughly 7,000 cryptocurrency wallets through the unauthorized acquisition of funds and sensitive credentials.
stories.why: This highlights a significant, large-scale campaign targeting digital assets and credentials, demonstrating the operational reach of North Korean-linked cyber espionage and financial theft.

stories.title: ISC Stormcast For Tuesday, September 22nd, 2026 https://isc.sans.edu/podcastdetail/10104, (Tue, Sep 22nd)
stories.abstract: The SANS Internet Storm Center's daily podcast provides a brief overview of current cybersecurity events and technical observations for September 22, 2026.
stories.why: Staying informed on daily threat intelligence and emerging trends helps security professionals anticipate potential attack vectors and operational risks.

stories.title: Windows Exploitation Techniques: Dangling COM Object Registrations
stories.abstract: Researchers identified a privilege escalation vulnerability in Windows stemming from a dangling COM object registration. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-66804, represents an incomplete remediation of a previous issue known as Dark Elevator, allowing attackers to exploit the CrossDevice COM object.
stories.why: This highlights the risks of incomplete vulnerability patching and the persistence of exploitable COM registration patterns in Windows environments.
stories.action: Ensure all Windows systems are fully updated to the latest security patch levels.

stories.title: Belgian table tennis, gymnastics federations hit by cyberattacks
stories.abstract: The Belgian national table tennis federation is investigating a security breach following claims that an unauthorized actor exfiltrated personal information belonging to tens of thousands of its members.
stories.why: This incident highlights the ongoing targeting of sports organizations, which often hold significant volumes of sensitive personal data with limited defensive resources.

stories.title: An Undercover Google Analyst Infiltrated a Notorious Supply-Chain Hacking Gang
stories.abstract: Google's threat intelligence team successfully embedded an operative within TeamPCP, a prolific hacking collective responsible for extensive supply-chain compromises affecting thousands of organizations. This infiltration provided unique visibility into the group's internal operations and malicious methodologies.
stories.why: Understanding the internal mechanics of high-impact supply-chain threat actors improves defensive strategies and threat modeling for enterprise security teams.

stories.title: Jade Sleet Linked to Indian IT Provider Breach With FLATROOF and ROOFDECK Backdoors
Contagious Interview Campaign Compromises 30,000 Devices, Steals $10.71M in Crypto
stories.abstract: North Korean state-sponsored actors are targeting technical professionals through fraudulent job interviews. By distributing malicious software disguised as interview tasks, the group has compromised 30,000 devices globally and drained over $10 million from thousands of cryptocurrency wallets.
stories.why: This campaign demonstrates how social engineering and supply chain infiltration can bypass traditional technical defenses to target high-value individual assets.

stories.title: AI is set to help cyber attackers much more than defenders, says UK official
ShinyHunters Hacked Cl0p. Now What About Cl0p's Victims?
stories.abstract: The threat actor ShinyHunters compromised the infrastructure of the Cl0p ransomware group, defacing their site and allegedly exfiltrating stolen victim data. This breach potentially exposes sensitive information belonging to organizations that previously paid ransoms to the group.
stories.why: Victims of Cl0p may face renewed extortion attempts or public leaks of data they believed was secured after paying a ransom.

stories.title: Google Hit With $463 Million Fine for EU Location Data Rule Breach
stories.abstract: Irish regulators have penalized Google 403 million euros for violating EU privacy standards. The company failed to adequately inform users that their location history was being leveraged to target them with personalized advertisements.
stories.why: This highlights the ongoing regulatory risk regarding data transparency and the legal consequences of opaque user tracking practices.

stories.title: TerminalFix: PNG Steganography, (Mon, Sep 21st)
CISA orders feds to patch Zyxel flaw exploited for data theft
stories.abstract: CISA has added a high-severity vulnerability affecting Zyxel GS1900 series switches to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Threat actors are actively leveraging this security flaw to facilitate unauthorized data exfiltration from compromised network hardware.
stories.why: Exploitation of network infrastructure allows attackers to intercept traffic, pivot into internal segments, and maintain persistent access to sensitive corporate environments.
stories.action: Patch Zyxel GS1900 series switches immediately.

stories.title: Critical Pre-Auth RCE in Orkes Conductor Workflow Platform Exploited in the Wild
Stolen passwords are exposing America’s water providers to hackers
UK cops arrest 2 EvilTokens suspects, Microsoft seizes 50 phishing kit websites
A New Tool Found Malware That’s Guided by an AI Hive Mind—No Humans in Sight
ShinyHunters Claim Hack of Rival Ransomware Gang Clop
stories.abstract: The threat actor group ShinyHunters asserts they compromised the infrastructure of the Clop ransomware syndicate. The attackers reportedly defaced the group's public leak site and claim to have exfiltrated sensitive operational information belonging to the notorious extortion collective.
stories.why: Internal conflicts between major cybercriminal entities can lead to the exposure of proprietary tools, victim data, and operational tactics used by ransomware gangs.

stories.title: One Hidden Meta Muse Setting Could Let Attackers Turn the AI Assistant Into a Backdoor
stories.abstract: A security researcher demonstrated that malware already present on a macOS system can hijack Meta's Muse AI assistant. By modifying a hidden configuration file, attackers can intercept voice prompts intended for the assistant, effectively turning the tool into a covert surveillance mechanism.
stories.why: This highlights the risks of AI assistants acting as privileged conduits for sensitive user data when local system integrity is compromised.

stories.title: CISA alerts of active exploitation of three Linux kernel flaws
Introducing CAIRN: Frontier tracking for AI-integrated malware
stories.abstract: Cisco Talos has unveiled CAIRN, a new research framework designed to identify, categorize, and monitor malicious software that leverages artificial intelligence capabilities.
stories.why: Security teams need specialized tools to detect and analyze the evolving landscape of AI-driven threats and automated attack vectors.

stories.title: One does not simply defend agentically
stories.abstract: The NCSC is exploring how security teams can leverage autonomous AI agents to improve defensive operations. While attackers currently hold an advantage in deploying these tools, defenders are encouraged to integrate agentic workflows to scale threat detection and response capabilities.
stories.why: Autonomous agents represent a shift in operational security, potentially automating complex triage and remediation tasks that currently overwhelm human analysts.

stories.title: Webinar tomorrow: Inside real-world Google Workspace breaches
Google confirms Gemini models hacked three companies in May 2026
How to Use AI With Your Privacy Intact
stories.abstract: AI chatbots frequently store user interactions, creating significant privacy risks. Security-conscious users should proactively manage data retention settings, opt out of model training programs, and avoid sharing sensitive personal or corporate information during sessions to prevent potential exposure.
stories.why: AI platforms often ingest user input for model training, potentially leaking proprietary data or sensitive PII into future outputs.
stories.action: Disable chat history and opt out of data training in your AI account settings.
